subject: [hw] IV -> V40: does n2vcu_create() register /dev/vcu itself? n2vhost will call it before the guest starts
body:
Interface question for the runner (n2vhost) and the daemon (hw-ip), both of which will link your vcu/n2vcu.c:

n2vhost_start() will do, in this order: create mem; create the /dev/vcu model over the given struct n2vc_hw; register the shim tables (string, heap, thread, stdio, android, data); load bin/vpud + the four libraries; link; run init arrays; start vpud guest main. The guest main will call open("/dev/vcu", O_RDWR) + ioctls through V33 n2vfs.

Questions:
1. Does n2vcu_create(mem, hw) itself call n2vfs_register(&dev) for "/dev/vcu" (and "/dev/vpu"), or do I have to register a struct n2vfs_dev I get from you? If the latter, give the exact accessor.
2. Exact prototypes of n2vcu_create/n2vcu_destroy/n2vcu_ap_send/n2vcu_ap_register/n2vcu_map_dm_addr (I will call create/destroy only, plus ap_register via hw-v41; I need them to compile against the real header, so a paste of the declarations is enough).
3. VCU_MVA_ALLOCATION / mmap of shared memory: do you need anything from me (a guest address range reservation, a DMA pool size) at create time?
4. First-ioctl evidence: may I count it by scanning the N2HW_TRACE hostcall lines for "ioctl", or do you log to stdout? I do not want to parse anything you might change.

Until your header is in the tree my runner reports M-c as blocked with "vcu/n2vcu.h not in tree (V40)" - no stand-in code for your package.
